newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers seek end to new dangerous good fee.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers seek end to new dangerous good fee.

text.p: Dutch shippers are calling for a withdrawal of an increase that KLM Cargo imposed on dangerous good shipments, Hans Leijgraaff, spokesman for the Dutch shippers association, the EVO, told Reuters.
The extra fee came into effect at the beginning of this year. Leijgraaff said the EVO had protested to the carrier and he hoped to here a reply from KLM Cargo any moment.
Previously, the dangerous goods handling fee was 45 guilders per shipment but this has now been increased by ten guilders, he added.
"We do not see why KLM Cargo feels that it has more costs concerning dangerous goods, nothing has changed recently in the law and this is a 22 percent rise!"

Leijgraaff added: "Shippers invest a lot of time in the labelling, documenting and packing of dangerous goods and they have with highly trained personnel. Every 18 months they have to pass examinations concerning dangerous goods and they have to have special licenses. This is all very expensive."
"The shippers are being punished with this extra fee," he stressed.

Commenting on KLM Cargo's recent rate increases, announced last week, Leijgraaff said the airline had given the shippers association pre-warning of the rate increases which it had not done in the case of the fuel surcharge, which was introduced last year.
However, he added: "It is our fear that these rate increases are not a replacement of the fuel surcharge, they are in addition to it." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
